official.deadline_note: 15 January applies to summer admission (start August/September, non-EU applicants; EU applicants 1 March). Winter admission uses 15 September for non-EU applicants - that deadline has passed for the January/February intake, so the next scholarship-relevant date is 15 January 2027. Non-EU applicants who also hold permanent residence in Denmark may apply by the later EU deadline.
official.application_cycle: Summer admission: application round opens 1 November, non-EU deadline 15 January for start August/September. Winter admission: round opens 24 August 2026, non-EU deadline 15 September for start January/February.
official.status_note: Aarhus University states: 'Only applicants who have applied for a Master's degree programme no later than 15 January (summer admission) and 15 September (winter admission) will be considered for a tuition waiver/scholarship.' As of the verification date the 15 September 2026 winter deadline has passed; the summer admission round opens 1 November 2026 and its scholarship deadline is 15 January 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: 'The content of a scholarship varies. In some cases, the scholarship is a full or partly tuition waiver. In other cases, the tuition waiver includes a monthly grant towards living expenses, typically but not always for the duration of your Master's degree programme.' Faculty of Arts and Aarhus BSS: tuition fee waiver + monthly grant towards living expenses. Faculty of Natural Sciences and Faculty of Technical Sciences: tuition fee waiver only (Aarhus University has 100% tuition fee waivers available in Natural and Technical Sciences).
benefits: In some cases, the scholarship is a full or partly tuition waiver

A full waiver covers the published annual tuition fee: EUR 13000 per year (60 ECTS) for Faculty of Arts and Aarhus BSS programmes and EUR 17300 per year for Faculty of Natural Sciences and Faculty of Technical Sciences programmes at 2026/2027 rates

For Natural and Technical Sciences: 'The waivers will be awarded to the most qualified and talented students.'

Living-expense grant: 'the scholarship may not cover all your living expenses in Denmark'

'When you apply for a Master's degree programme at Aarhus University, you also apply for a scholarship. No additional documents are required.'
official.application_route: Submit the regular online admission application for a Master's degree programme at Aarhus University by 15 January (summer) or 15 September (winter); the scholarship assessment is automatic and no separate application exists.
official.citizenship_residency: 'EU/EEA/Swiss students cannot apply for scholarships at AU.' Scholarships can only be awarded to applicants liable to pay tuition fees at Aarhus University.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the Danish state scholarships are aimed at non-EU/EEA/Swiss applicants who are liable to pay tuition fees; EU/EEA/Swiss citizens are excluded.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No subject restriction is published, but the scholarship is 'connected very specifically to your Master's degree programme and cannot be transferred to another degree programme at AU', and award levels vary by faculty (Arts and BSS add a monthly grant; Natural and Technical Sciences offer tuition waivers only).
official.duration: The monthly grant is paid 'typically but not always for the duration of your Master's degree programme'. English-taught Master's degree programmes are 120 ECTS with tuition fees stated per year (60 ECTS) and paid per semester (30 ECTS).
official.description: Aarhus University offers a limited number of Danish state scholarships for non-EU students, financed solely by the Danish state - the university has no scholarship funds of its own. The scholarship takes the form of a full or partial tuition fee waiver, with a monthly grant towards living expenses at the Faculty of Arts and Aarhus BSS. Applying for admission to a Master's programme by the stated deadline automatically triggers scholarship assessment; no separate application exists.
official.program_type: Danish state scholarship (tuition fee waiver, with monthly living-expense grant in some faculties)
official.english_requirement: IELTS Academic: minimum 6.5 overall with at least 6.0 in each subscore (IELTS one skill retake not accepted). TOEFL iBT: minimum 83 with at least 20 in each subscore for results achieved before 21 January 2026; minimum 4.5 with at least 4.0 in each subscore for results after that date (TOEFL ITP, Essentials, MyBest Scores and paper-based tests not accepted). Cambridge English Qualifications: minimum 180 points on the Cambridge English Scale (C2 Proficiency 190, C1 Advanced grade A-C, B2 First grade A). Tests must be no more than two years old on the day the application portal opens. Exemptions: completed Bachelor's or Master's degree from a university in Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the UK, the USA or Ireland taught in English, a Bachelor's degree from a Danish university (admission after 2008), an English-taught Master's from a Danish university, or qualifying upper secondary examinations. Duolingo English Test and Pearson PTE are not accepted.

verification.notes: Scholarship structure (full/partial tuition waiver; monthly living grant only at Faculty of Arts and Aarhus BSS), non-EU eligibility, automatic assessment, 15 January/15 September deadlines, selection process, application fee, tuition rates for 2026/27 and English test minimums were all confirmed directly on masters.au.dk pages (scholarships page revised 08.07.2026). Aarhus University does not publish a figure for the monthly living-expense grant anywhere on its scholarship pages, so the amount fields are null rather than estimated.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no scholarship form: your admission application to an Aarhus University Master's programme is the scholarship application, so the whole contest is decided by whether you file by 15 January 2027 for the August/September 2027 intake (15 September governs the February winter intake, already passed this cycle). The prize is a tuition waiver worth EUR 13,000 per year at Arts and BSS or EUR 17,300 per year at Natural and Technical Sciences at 2026/27 rates, and only Faculty of Arts and Aarhus BSS add a monthly living-expense grant on top. With typically one or two awards per programme and no published grant amount, treat this as a long-shot bonus: budget living costs, travel and settling-in money yourself, and remember the 150 EUR application fee that buys up to three applications but is refunded only if you enrol.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU/EEA/Swiss applicants with excellent transcripts applying to Aarhus Arts or BSS Master's programmes, where the waiver comes with a monthly living grant.
application_readiness_checklist: Pay the 150 EUR (1125 DKK) non-EU application fee through the AU web shop and upload the receipt to each application - unpaid applications are not processed
Sit IELTS or TOEFL early: the result must be under two years old on the day the application portal opens, and Duolingo and PTE are rejected outright
Assemble the official diploma, transcript of records, an official grading-scale description and linked or stamped course descriptions for every course taken
File the admission application by 15 January (summer) or 15 September (winter) - scholarship consideration cannot be added afterwards
Upload no extra scholarship documents; AU explicitly asks applicants not to add documentation for the scholarship
common_rejection_risks: Applying after the 15 January/15 September cut-off, which removes scholarship consideration even when admission is still possible
Missing the very short acceptance window for the offer that arrives together with the letter of admission
Assuming EU/EEA/Swiss citizenship still allows an application, or expecting the Danish SU grant scheme to cover the tuition liability
Counting on the monthly grant to fund the whole stay - AU warns it may not cover all living expenses, especially settling-in costs
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living expenses beyond the monthly grant (AU states the grant may not cover all living costs), travel to Denmark and settling-in costs such as room deposit, furniture, bicycle or bus card. Tuition-waiver-only recipients must additionally document sufficient funds to support themselves for the student residence permit. Books and course material are not covered by tuition.
document_audit: The application fee receipt must be uploaded to each of the applications individually, and the full amount must be paid by the deadline
The diploma must clearly state when the Bachelor's degree was completed; unfinished degrees require current official transcripts instead
The grading scale must show both the lowest passing grade and the highest grade, and the course descriptions must be official (direct links or university stamp and signature)
Documents not issued in Danish, Norwegian, Swedish or English must be translated by an authorised translator or the issuing university
alerts: The scholarship is tied to the specific Master's programme and cannot be transferred to another AU degree programme

At Natural and Technical Sciences, waiver decisions continue through March - do not decline your admission offer before 1 April (summer) or 1 November (winter), or you may forfeit a waiver that was still in process
Until a Danish tax card is in place after arrival, 55% of the monthly grant is withheld as tax and only regulated later
Receiving a tuition waiver without a monthly grant still obliges you to document sufficient funds for the student residence permit
The result of scholarship assessment arrives as either an offer or a tuition fee notification alongside the letter of admission
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: File one online admission application per target programme in the AU application portal with the fee receipt and required documents by the deadline; AU assesses scholarship eligibility alongside the academic assessment and returns the waiver offer or a tuition fee notification with the letter of admission, with a very short acceptance deadline.
